analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/inference.md:416–1210 and supplied patch orientation against the canonical index and detailed T-041. The visible change at head:810–815 accepts variable-frame-rate video, indexes frames using nominalFrameRate, and retains the official 2 FPS sample; head:829 no longer lists variable frame rate as a deterministic refusal. This expands adversarial media input at TB-007 but does not itself establish a vulnerability. Documented decoded-frame and prepared-pixel caps, media reservations, scoped MLX fault handling, exclusion of media from prefix reuse, and target-only media decoding remain unchanged (815–835). Surrounding ownership, retirement, authenticated cache scope, usage, calibration and admission descriptions do not establish new authorization, encryption, billing or cache-isolation regressions (A-001, T-010, T-028, T-041, T-053, T-056).
Integration must verify GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset's actual variable-frame-rate handling: validation of finite positive nominalFrameRate, bounds on frames scanned/decoder work and cancellation, and consistency between sampled frames, timestamps and GLM5NextVisionBudget.videoTokenCeiling. A retained RGB cap alone does not prove bounded scan work, but missing implementation here is not evidence of a missing control. Also reconcile the inline-video-label change oriented at head:1896–1899 with MediaIngest and decoder validation; that source range is not replayed in these units and its patch is truncated. These are coverage limits requiring source integration, not independently supported findings. No deployment or full-artifact qualification is inferred from the documentation.
